scope: Experimental single-domain finite-deformation static analysis with a tabulated isotropic elastic-plastic material, fixed FACE support, proportional surface loading, bounded nonlinear increments, solver-derived plastic-strain/energy history, and paginated final material fields.

lanes.acceptance: The sealed nonlinear_static request admits only one domain, fixed supports, an explicit isotropic_elastic_plastic material, a strictly increasing true-stress/plastic-strain isotropic-hardening table beginning at yield and zero plastic strain, supported loads, bounded steps/increments, and mandatory plastic-strain/energy results before geometry transfer.

The version-bound CalculiX adapter deterministically emits the admitted isotropic hardening table and requests PEEQ, ENER, and ELSE at frequency one in every nonlinear step, without changing the existing NLGEOM, amplitude, increment, quota, or cleanup architecture.

Every accepted converged increment has complete finite nonnegative PEEQ, energy-density, and total-internal-energy data. Missing or malformed material output fails closed. Final equivalent-plastic-strain and strain-energy-density fields are digest-verified and paginated without exposing raw native files.

A native 100 x 10 x 10 mm axial coupon at 30 kN separates elastic and elastic-plastic response, yields the mesh, recovers finite plastic strain and energy, and balances the axial support reaction within 3 N.

A two-step 30 kN load-unload-reload coupon demonstrates linear elastic unload/reload branches, matched residual intercepts, residual plastic strain, nondecreasing PEEQ, path equilibrium, recoverable-energy release/return, and external-work/internal-energy consistency.

Monotonic and load-unload-reload histories use three meshes with strictly increasing actual element counts. Because separately generated unstructured tetrahedral meshes need not contract monotonically, the declared gate is a bounded medium-to-fine whole-history norm for displacement, PEEQ, and internal energy plus bounded cyclic residual/stiffness metrics.

Maximum nonlinear increments 0.10, 0.075, and 0.05 produce contracting whole-history displacement, PEEQ, and internal-energy changes for monotonic and load-unload-reload coupons. Fine cyclic residual and branch-stiffness changes also contract and remain bounded.

Deliberate increment exhaustion and active cancellation occur only after complete positive PEEQ/ENER/ELSE frames exist while the provider is running. Both paths expose no normalized result or field pages, remove their exact native directory, and resist late-result resurrection.

An analytically bracketed solid cantilever compares a monotonic sub-yield path with an overload-return path ending at the same applied load and reaction. The overload path retains root-localized PEEQ, larger fitted root-zone chord rotation and energy, persistent PEEQ on return, and equilibrium throughout the recorded reaction history.

Every SIM-7B result remains experimental, requires engineer review, carries explicit material/geometric nonlinearity warnings, and denies engineering use. The matrix does not claim reordered multi-axis loading, multi-domain material nonlinearity, advanced constitutive laws, limit-point continuation, or any non-Windows runtime qualification.

An independent qualified engineer approves the material law and units, analytical assumptions, path definitions, field reductions, energy interpretation, convergence norms and tolerances, lifecycle evidence, limitations, exact public commit, and digest-bound automated evidence before any engineering-use promotion.
